mca.books.death.author: Ozzie the Warrior
mca.books.death.0: §fI couldn't count how many times my family has been blown to pieces by creepers. How are they still around, you may ask? Easy! I, dear reader, have discovered a cure for death itself! And through this book, I can share it with you.
mca.books.death.1:
§f§lGraves§r§f
§r§fWhen a villager dies, his corpse is buried in the nearest grave. So make sure to keep a plot in your graveyard empty.
mca.books.death.2:
§f§lSummoning Grim§r§f
Unfortunately, the only entity capable of defeating death is death itself: the Grim Reaper. To summon him, you must build an altar consisting of 3 obsidian columns that are at least 2 blocks high. They may be higher if you like.
mca.books.death.3:
§f§lSummoning Grim 2§r§f
In the center you have to place the sacrifice, an emerald block.
mca.books.death.4:
§f§lSummoning Grim 3§r§f
After building the altar, wait until night and light all 3 columns. When you're ready to fight, light the emerald block and run!
mca.books.death.5:
§f§lFighting Grim§r§f
Grim is tough. Use full diamond armor, lots of potions, and lots of enchantments. He can:
- Fly
- Block attacks
- Blind you
- Move your items
- Teleport
mca.books.death.6:
§f§lFighting Grim 2§r§f
If you hit Grim while he's blocking, he will teleport behind you and strike. Do not try to use arrows or poison, he is immune!
mca.books.death.7:
§f§lFighting Grim 3§r§f
When Grim loses too much health he will teleport into the air and begin healing. While healing, he will summon his minions from the underworld to fight you.
mca.books.death.8:
§f§lFighting Grim 4§r§f
When Grim is healed, he will continue attacking you, but he won't be able to heal again for 3 minutes and 30 seconds. Each time Grim heals, he will not be able to restore as much health as he did previously.
mca.books.death.9:
§f§lThe Scythe§r§f
Once you land the lethal hit, he falls back into the void and leaves his Scythe behind. The Scythe, feeling ice cold on touch, is a mighty tool. Strike down a villager to charge the scythe, then transfer the stored soul to the gravestone.
mca.books.death.10:
§f§lThe Scythe 2§r§f
But your friend will rise infected, as the time underground left some marks. You can probably heal him somehow, my friend Richard once wrote a book about this topic.
mca.books.death.11:
§f§lStaff Of Life§r§f
However, there is another, more peaceful solution. The Staff of Life! Instead of a poor soul, it uses the Nether Stars concentrated power to revive.
mca.books.death.12:
§f§lStaff Of Life 2§r§f
The Staff is a powerful item that can revive people. Unlike the Scythe, it is even capable of erasing any sickness from the revived person.
mca.books.romance.author: Gerry the Librarian
mca.books.romance.0:
§lIntroduction§r
Interaction is key to building relationships and finding the love of your life. I've happily written this book in order to share my knowledge of interaction, love, and, unfortunately, divorce, to anyone who may need a little push in the right direction.
mca.books.romance.1:
§lPersonalities§r
When speaking to any villager, you'll notice they have a personality. Pay close attention to this! Some people like jokes more, some love a hug. Some personalities are more obvious than others. Hover over the personality to see some hints.
mca.books.romance.2:
§lMoods§r
Every person has a mood, which is always apparent when speaking to them. Moods can change throughout the day, and determine how likely a villager is to like certain interactions.
mca.books.romance.3:
§lMoods 2§r
The death of a villager seems to put those nearby in bad moods. Taxing also gradually decreases the moods of everyone. Gifts and successful interactions are known to boost moods.
mca.books.romance.4:
§lInteracting§r
Choose wisely when interacting with a villager, based on their mood and personality! If choosing a romantic interaction, be sure that the villager you are talking to likes you a lot.
mca.books.romance.5:
§lInteracting pt. 2§r
Don't be annoying! Talking to someone for too long will bore them, and your interactions may stop succeeding. If this happens, simply wait some time before trying to talk to them again.
mca.books.romance.6:
§lGifts§r
Gifts are another great way to win someone's friendship. But again, be careful who you gift what. A fisherman loves fish, but oh my, don't ever gift a smelly fish to a noble lady.
mca.books.romance.7:
§lMarriage§r
To get married, simply gift a villager a wedding ring once you feel you have reached the highest relationship level.
mca.books.romance.8:
§lDivorce§r
Unfortunately, sometimes it is best to split from your spouse and move on. To do this, look for a cleric to get divorce papers. Then talk to your spouse.
mca.books.romance.9:
§lDivorce pt. 2§r
Alternatively you can end the marriage without papers, they will not be happy tho.
mca.books.family.author: Leanne the Cleric
mca.books.family.0: Children, are our future! Make sure to have as many as you possibly can.§rNot only do you get to experience the joy of raising a child, but once they are past the baby stage, put them to work!
mca.books.family.1:
§lBabies§r
When you are married, simply approach your spouse and offer to 'Procreate'. After a short dance, you'll be the proud owner of a new baby boy or girl (or maybe even both)!
mca.books.family.2:
§lGrowth§r
Babies take time to grow, make sure to hold them until they are ready, or give them to your spouse to take care of. Once a baby is ready to grow, you may place it on the ground and it will grow into a child!
mca.books.family.3:
§lAdolescence§r
Children will grow slowly. However, the magical properties of Golden Apples are said to accelerate any child's growth. I have yet to try this myself.
mca.books.family.4:
§lChores§r
Any child can farm, cut wood, hunt, and fish. You'll need to provide them with the tools they need to do so. If a tool breaks and the child doesn't have another, they will have no choice but to stop working.
mca.books.family.5:
§lAdulthood§r
As sad as it may be, children will eventually grow into adults.. Adults can be married off by using Matchmaker's Rings, or they will eventually get married on their own.
mca.books.rose_gold.author: William the Miner
mca.books.rose_gold.0:
§lWarning!
TOP SECRET§r
This manual is the property of William Mining Co.§rIf you are not a William Mining Co. employee, please refrain from reading this manual and return promptly to William the Miner.
mca.books.rose_gold.1: Ah, rose gold - a lovely combination of copper and gold that smelts into a pinkish-orange metal. Most use it as an alternative to gold for crafting rings as it is much less expensive. However, it has some interesting qualities that are easy to miss.
mca.books.rose_gold.2:
§lCreating Ingots§r
Crush some raw gold and copper ore to obtain a blend, which already shares the pinkish color of rose gold. Then, smelt the blend in the blast furnace and cast it into an ingot.
mca.books.rose_gold.3:
§Usage§r
Rose gold is a very soft metal, so it is not suitable for tools or armor. However, it makes for a great material for rings. Or rose gold blocks, if you're into that.
mca.books.infection.author: Richard the Zombie
mca.books.infection.0: Good, day, readers! I've written this book so that you may not end up suffering the same fate as I. Although I caught the infection, I was luckily able to keep all of my mental faculties.
mca.books.infection.1:
§lWhat is the Infection?§r
I discovered a long time ago that the zombies that appear at night were once villagers! Newly infected villagers slowly turn green, feel unwell and may be unable to speak properly!
mca.books.infection.2:
§lCuring§r
Contrary to popular belief, any infected villager can be cured. Gift a villager a golden apple to cure an ongoing infection. If the infection turned the villager into a zombie already you must first weaken the zombie with a potion, then apply the golden apple.
mca.books.infection.3:
§lCuring 2§r
Any other zombies you see unfortunately are too far gone, and cannot be cured.
mca.books.infection.4:
§lCuring 3§r
Zombies will take a couple of minutes to be fully cured. Villagers who were recently infected, though, and haven't had time to degrade into a full zombie, will be cured instantly!
mca.books.infection.5:
§lWarnings§r
Villagers are highly susceptible to infection, decrease the risk of infection by building an infirmary!
mca.books.blueprint.author: Carl the Builder
mca.books.blueprint.0: §fWe villager can farm. We can smith tools and armor. We can read, brew, enchant and so much more. But there is one thing we lack the knowledge for: construction!
mca.books.blueprint.1: §fOn your journey, you probably come across several villages full of small, impractical, and barely decorated houses. How should a village ever evolve into something bigger?
mca.books.blueprint.2:
§f§lBlueprint§r§f
That's why I'm wandering across the planet, helping villages I encounter on my travels. And you could too! Craft yourself a blueprint using blue dye and paper and check out the catalog of buildings every village needs but can't build on their own.
mca.books.blueprint.3:
§f§lRequirements§r§f
A buildings usually requires a minimum size. You can't just plug everything into a shed. Then you have to make sure that all the block requirements are fulfilled.
mca.books.blueprint.4:
§f§lFinish§r§f
Once done, hit 'Add Building' and watch how villagers integrate it into the village.
mca.books.blueprint.5:
§f§lRanks§r§f
But you don't need to be selfless! The more advanced your village is, the higher your rank gets. Ever dreamed to live a life of a noble? A mayor? Or even a King?
mca.books.cult_0.author: Lucas the Devotee
mca.books.cult_0.0: A long time ago, a being from another world came to this planet, sharing its wisdom as it travels across the land… This entity was called Sirben the 99.
mca.books.cult_0.1: Despite good intentions, its knowledge was too much for our minds to comprehend, some people didn't listen, but those who did were changed, to never be the same again…
mca.books.cult_0.2: Their minds, shattered by the truths Sirben said, became obsessed, and they passed “the sacred words” on to the next generations. Everyone who gains this erratic behavior receives the “Sirben” trait.
mca.books.cult_0.3: Until this day, some people say they still can hear its whispers…
mca.books.cult_1.author: Evelyn the Seeker
mca.books.cult_1.0: The Sirben cult speaks of a higher power that transcends our world, a being that exists beyond our understanding of time and space.
mca.books.cult_1.1: Through meditation and ritual, cultists attempt to commune with this entity, hoping to gain insight into its unknowable nature and the secrets of the universe.
mca.books.cult_1.2: But with this knowledge comes a price - a madness that grips the mind and twists the soul. Those who follow Sirben's teachings must tread carefully, lest they lose themselves in the pursuit of forbidden truths.
mca.books.cult_1.3: Yet even as the world scoffs at their beliefs, the cultists remain steadfast in their devotion. For they know that beyond the veil of reality lies a realm of infinite wonder, where the mysteries of the cosmos are laid bare for those with the courage to seek them.
mca.books.cult_2.author: Barnaby the Adventurer
mca.books.cult_2.0: In order to summon the ancient cultists, one must perform a ritual at midnight during a snowfall. But be warned, this is no ordinary ritual - it requires the milk of a goat!
mca.books.cult_2.1: That's right, you must milk a goat at midnight in the middle of a snowstorm! It sounds strange, but it's the only way to wake the ancient cultists from their slumber.
mca.books.cult_2.2: But be careful, for these undead cultists are not to be taken lightly. They may be aggressive towards you once awakened, and will stop at nothing to protect their secrets.
mca.books.cult_2.3: If you're brave enough to face them, though, there's a chance they'll drop the secret words of the Sirbens upon their defeat. And with those words, you'll unlock a new level of understanding about the mysteries of this world and beyond.
mca.books.cult_ancient.author: The Ancient Sirbens
mca.letter.condolence:
%s,

It is with great regret that we have to inform you of %s's death.

Yours sincerely,
the mayor of %s
mca.books.supporters.author: The Community
mca.books.expansion_guide.author: The village chroniclers
mca.books.expansion_guide.0: This guide explains everything the expansion adds to MCA: villagers with needs, belongings and schedules, planned construction, a real economy and more.
mca.books.expansion_guide.1: Each system can be turned on or off in mca.json: villagerNeeds, villagerActionQueue, villagerProperty, villagerWorkOrders and villagerEconomy. The visuals have their own options.
mca.books.expansion_guide.2:
§lHuman-like villagers§r
With squidward models, the squidwardHumanLikeModels option gives villagers the player's body, with MCA's skin, face, clothes and hair.
mca.books.expansion_guide.3:
§l3D layers§r
squidward3dLayers turns hat, jacket, sleeves and pants into small cubes when a villager is close. player3dLayers does the same for players.
mca.books.expansion_guide.4:
§lHeight§r
The height gene sets each villager's size (squidwardHeightVariation) and children grow in stages. With Fresh Animations, turn on freshAnimationsIntegration.
mca.books.expansion_guide.5:
§lWork§r
During work hours a villager walks to their job site and works at it for a while, playing their profession's animation, then rests, strolls and chats.
mca.books.expansion_guide.6: Right-click a villager: the buttons appear in a circle, with icons. Talk and Interact are the two main paths.
mca.books.expansion_guide.7:
§lSubmenus§r
Interact has gift, trade, inventory, family tree, Commands (follow, stay, ride), Orders and Professions. Turning off radialInteractMenu brings back the classic menu.
mca.books.expansion_guide.8: Six meters from 0 to 100 drop over time: Hunger, Thirst, Energy, Social, Fun and Safety. Low meters become thoughts that weigh on the mood.
mca.books.expansion_guide.9:
§lHunger§r
Villagers eat from their inventory or a chest at home: give bread, meat or other food. Working makes them hungrier. Starving costs health down to half a heart, never death.
mca.books.expansion_guide.10:
§lThirst§r
They drink standing next to a cauldron with water: put cauldrons in the village.
§lEnergy§r
Refills by sleeping in bed at night. Without a bed they nap anywhere.
mca.books.expansion_guide.11:
§lSocial§r
Rises when talking to you, to other villagers and at the bell's meeting point.
§lFun§r
Free time and favorite buildings. Work is tiring.
mca.books.expansion_guide.12:
§lSafety§r
Drops when monsters come close. Recovers at home, near guards or golems. A critical meter makes a villager drop their routine to deal with it.
mca.books.expansion_guide.13: The meters show on the interaction screen: hover one to see how to fill it. Couples who sleep together are happier.
mca.books.expansion_guide.14: Like in The Sims, every villager has a queue of what their schedule, needs and your orders ask for, and does the most urgent first. The queue shows above their head.
mca.books.expansion_guide.15:
§lOrders§r
The Orders menu: eat, drink, sleep, go home, work, socialize or relax. Each entry shows its reason and urgency; click an entry to cancel it.
mca.books.expansion_guide.16: With the Villager Editor, the Schedule tab shows a villager's day: Idle, Work, Meet, Rest and Play. Pick a preset, or click and drag on the timeline to paint the hours.
mca.books.expansion_guide.17: A custom schedule is saved with Done; Reset brings back the original. Warnings show what is missing: without a job site or meeting point, the villager stays idle.
mca.books.expansion_guide.18: Beds, job sites, chests, doors and trapdoors belong to someone. Villagers own their bed, job site and home, with everything inside. You own what you place.
mca.books.expansion_guide.19:
§lWho may enter§r
Spouse, family, the mayor and friends with 50 hearts or more (except for beds). A home's door locks while all of its residents are inside.
mca.books.expansion_guide.20:
§lPadlock§r
Recipe: 3 nuggets in an arc over 3 ingots. Use it on your own chest or door to lock it. Sneaking with an empty hand takes it back.
mca.books.expansion_guide.21:
§lForcing§r
Sneak with an empty hand and hold use for 3 seconds.
§lLockpick§r
2 nuggets diagonally and 1 stick. Takes 5 seconds, is silent and one is used up when it opens.
mca.books.expansion_guide.22:
§lCrowbar§r
4 ingots shaped as a hook. Opens at once and destroys the padlock, but it is loud: whoever hears it comes to look. Villagers replace the padlock after a day.
mca.books.expansion_guide.23:
§lWitnesses§r
Villagers see crimes up to 24 blocks away (half if you sneak, half again in the dark). A witness loses 10 hearts with you, the owner 25.
mca.books.expansion_guide.24: Craft a Blueprint (paper around blue dye) and use it in a village. The Plan Work button opens a free camera above the village.
mca.books.expansion_guide.25:
§lControls§r
WASD, Space and Shift fly. Drag with the right button to look. Scroll changes the altitude. Keys 1 to 4: tools. Tab: list of jobs.
mca.books.expansion_guide.26:
§lDig [1]§r
Miners and builders clear the area and store what they dig.
§lBuild [2]§r
Builders fill the area with the chosen block, taken from the storage.
mca.books.expansion_guide.27:
§lWho may plan§r
Nobles or higher, or anyone holding a Villager Editor (then without materials). Pick Builder or Miner in a villager's Professions menu.
mca.books.expansion_guide.28:
§lBlueprints§r
Capture [4]: drag a box around something you built and name it. Blueprint [3]: pick a saved one, turn it with R and place it. Four come ready.
mca.books.expansion_guide.29: Builders clear the way, fetch every material from the storage and, once done, the building counts as one of the village's. There is also the /mca workorder command.
mca.books.expansion_guide.30: With villagerEconomy on, the village really produces. New professions gather resources: a jobless villager takes the job on finding a free station.
mca.books.expansion_guide.31:
§lStations§r
Chopping Block: flint over a log. Hunting Rack: stick, leather, stick over 3 planks. Forage Basket: wheat in a U shape.
mca.books.expansion_guide.32:
§lLumberjack§r
Fells trees near the block, picks up apples and sticks and replants saplings.
§lHunter§r
Hunts wild animals; spares named, leashed and penned ones and the last of a kind.
mca.books.expansion_guide.33:
§lForager§r
Picks wild berries without removing the bush, the tops of sugar cane and bamboo, mushrooms and flowers where there are many, and wild pumpkins and melons.
mca.books.expansion_guide.34:
§lFisherman§r
Fishes from the shore near the barrel.
§lMiner§r
Without jobs, takes sand, gravel and clay off the surface around a Sifting Sieve (plank, string, plank over two planks).
mca.books.expansion_guide.35: Gatherers work up to 24 blocks from their station and stop gathering an item once the village storage holds 128 of it.
mca.books.expansion_guide.36: Villagers at their job site produce in batches, with inputs from the workshop chest. The bakery (a butcher's) bakes bread from wheat; the mason makes bricks from cobblestone.
mca.books.expansion_guide.37: The toolsmith makes crowbars, axes and shovels; the armorer makes helmets and sometimes finds a diamond; the cleric makes redstone from rotten flesh. Recipes live in data/mca/production.
mca.books.expansion_guide.38:
§lThe split§r
The village's share follows the tax: at 30%, 30% goes to the workshop chest and the rest stays with the villager. Without a chest it all stays. Old item taxes are gone.
mca.books.expansion_guide.39:
§lWorkshop chest§r
It belongs to the workers and the haulers: opening it otherwise is theft. With full pockets, a villager takes their share to a chest in their own home.
mca.books.expansion_guide.40:
§lFarmer§r
Has no recipe: the village gets its share of the real harvest, in a workshop chest or one next to the composter.
mca.books.expansion_guide.41: The Hauler brings what workshops made to the storage and stocks each workshop with inputs for 5 batches, combining both on the same trip.
mca.books.expansion_guide.42: Villages with a storage and two or more workshops get a hauler from their jobless villagers, and one more for every 5 workshops. It can also be picked in the Professions menu.
mca.books.expansion_guide.43: Without a hauler, each craftsman fetches one batch of inputs from the storage every two days.
mca.books.expansion_guide.44: Holding the Villager Editor, the last villager under the crosshair shows their look and AI above their head, their path and the places they remember: bed, job site, meeting point, home.
mca.books.expansion_guide.45: The K key freezes or unfreezes their AI. In the editor, the Inspect tab shows genes, social, look, AI and places, and the Schedule tab edits their day.
mca.books.expansion_guide.46: With villagerSkills on, every villager gets better at their profession by working, from 0 to 100. The skill shows next to the profession on the interaction screen.
mca.books.expansion_guide.47:
§lSkill§r
A skilled hand works up to twice as fast, sometimes makes one more and finds rare things more often. Skilled smiths sometimes enchant what they make.
mca.books.expansion_guide.48:
§lIntelligence§r
An inherited gene sets how far (40 to 100) and how fast a villager learns. Children get smarter at School: a lectern, 4 wooden stairs and 4 bookshelves.
mca.books.expansion_guide.49:
§lVaried food§r
The same food again and again fills less and gets boring; variety cheers up. Villagers pick the food they ate least lately on their own.
mca.books.expansion_guide.50:
§lHome§r
Room per resident, light from torches or lanterns, decoration (pots, carpets, candles, bookshelves) and a chest make a home cozy. A cramped, dark home gets them down.
mca.books.expansion_guide.51:
§lDecisions§r
The jobless look for what they are best at. Gatherers without a tool take one from the storage. Hungry with nothing at home, they eat from it. Workshops make what is missing first.
mca.books.expansion_guide.52:
§lFree time§r
With villagerRoutines, villagers use what is around: they sit on stairs and slabs, chat with friends, read in the library, listen to music, look at items on display, pet the cat. Alone, they stay near others.
mca.books.expansion_guide.53: With villagerRequests on, the radial menu gets "Need any help?". The villager asks for a delivery and promises a reward taken from the chests in their home.
mca.books.expansion_guide.54:
§lReward§r
The villager sets the reward aside right when asking: it leaves the chest and is kept until you deliver. The more hearts you share, the more valuable an offer they make.
mca.books.expansion_guide.55:
§lDelivering§r
Bring the items and pick "Need any help?" again: you get the reward and hearts by difficulty. After 3 days the request runs out: the reward goes back home and you lose 3 hearts.
mca.books.expansion_guide.56:
§lSavings§r
On the first request, the home chests get the villager's savings, by profession. Later they grow with their share of the work. Requests and values live in data/mca/requests.
mca.books.expansion_guide.57:
§lHunts§r
Sometimes the request is to defeat monsters: zombies, spiders, skeletons, creepers, pillagers. The villager counts by your statistics; talk to them again when done.
mca.books.expansion_guide.58:
§lBoard§r
The Request Board (3 paper over 3 planks) brings a request from someone in the village who needs help. Sneaking lists your open requests. Up to 3 per village.
mca.books.expansion_guide.59:
§lHaggling§r
With villagerBarter, any villager sells what it carries for emeralds and buys food and what its workshop uses. Friends pay less. "What do you carry?" shows its inventory.
mca.books.expansion_guide.60: With villageProgression on, the village follows a path: Camp, Hamlet, Village, Thriving Village, Town and City. The Blueprint's Progress tab shows the stage and what is missing.
mca.books.expansion_guide.61:
§lThe path§r
Each stage asks for buildings, better houses, workshops and residents. Nothing is locked: any building works early. The path only suggests the order and tells when the village grows.
mca.books.expansion_guide.62:
§lHouses§r
Small House: one bed. Common: 2 beds, a chest and 30 floor. Big: 4 beds, 2 chests, a furnace and 80 floor. Huge: 6 beds, 3 chests, 6 decorations and 140 floor.
mca.books.expansion_guide.63:
§lWorkshops§r
Each work station is a place for one worker. A bakery with 3 smokers and room (15 floor per station) is level III and works with 3 butchers.
mca.books.expansion_guide.64:
§lIntegrations§r
With villagerRoutines, villagers use things from other mods. Each integration is a file in data/mca/opportunities: without the mod the file is skipped and nothing breaks.
mca.books.expansion_guide.65:
§lMusic§r
With Immersive Melodies, gift an instrument: the villager plays in free time, more so at the inn and the music store. Neighbors stop to listen, and others join in, in time.
mca.books.expansion_guide.66:
§lKitchen§r
With Farmer's Delight, a butcher at the inn cooks stews, soups and feasts. A feast set on the table gathers villagers: each takes a serving. Cabinets count as chests.
mca.books.expansion_guide.67:
§lWindows§r
Shutters: a trapdoor and a stick make two. Put them on the wall beside the window; closed, they cover it. Villagers open them in the morning, close them at night and light Beautify lamps.
mca.books.expansion_guide.68:
§lPlaced items§r
With Tabletop, V puts the held item down on a block. Villagers pick up instruments, play and put them back, eat the food and look at the rest. Workshops show their wares on tables.
